_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x17-ra-input.json; I opened no other file, ran no repository search and used no web or paid API.

hints.reason: Michael Jordan gives AIR via Air Jordan and JAM via Space Jam, two instantly familiar references with a real payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent shared-reference pair; text is accurate.

hints.reason: ANT through the familiar species name army ant and SOLDIER because soldiers serve in an army; clean and easy.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but fair; the army-ant name is instantly familiar.

hints.reason: Cupid shoots arrows (ARROW) and is the god of love (LOVE); obvious but tidy.

pairs.pair_note: Clear, easy clue; text accurate.

hints.reason: Both BAG and CAT come from the idiom 'let the cat out of the bag' (reveal a secret), a satisfying idiom-reversal clue.
hints.fix: BAG: In the saying, the cat stands for the secret and the bag is where it was hidden.

pairs.pair_note: Strong idiom clue; the BAG line is slightly muddled (the cat, not the secret, is in the bag), so a small rewrite is suggested.

hints.reason: Hershey's chocolate bar gives BAR and Hershey's Kisses give KISS; a fun brand double.

pairs.pair_note: Strong brand pair; text accurate.

hints.reason: Thriller the album includes 'Beat It' (BEAT) and the Thriller video's zombie dance gives ZOMBIE; iconic on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; both routes are iconic Michael Jackson knowledge.

hints.reason: Microsoft points to BILL via co-founder Bill Gates and to WINDOW via Windows; a nice indirect aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect clue; singular WINDOW vs Windows is fine.

hints.reason: Blood cells give BLOOD and prison cells give PRISON; a clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic double meaning; text accurate.

hints.reason: Chemistry studies chemical bonds (BOND) and couples in love are said to have chemistry (LOVE); a satisfying literal/figurative double.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning with a real aha.

hints.reason: A violin is played with a bow (BOW) and has strings (STRING); obvious but solid.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; ARCHERY would also fit but is no better.

hints.reason: Brushes have bristles (BRUSH) and pigs/boars have coarse bristles used in boar- and hog-bristle brushes (PIG); the pig side is real but takes a beat, and hedgehog or porcupine may tempt first.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are correct; PIG side is the weaker half, so a second opinion between PASS and BORDERLINE is reasonable.

hints.reason: Ribs form the rib cage (CAGE) and are prominent bones of the skeleton (SKELETON); easy and clean.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the singular RIB would also work since the phrase is 'rib cage'.

hints.reason: Niagara Falls gives FALL and sits on the Canada-U.S. border (CANADA); familiar and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strong place clue; text accurate.

hints.reason: Ford the carmaker gives CAR and Ford's Theatre, where Lincoln was shot, gives THEATER; a great two-domain aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent history/brand double; text accurate.

hints.reason: Alice in Wonderland's Caterpillar (CATERPILLAR) sits on the grow-or-shrink mushroom (MUSHROOM); an iconic, accurate scene.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent story clue; text matches the book.

hints.reason: Swiss cheese (CHEESE) and sponges (SPONGE) are both known for being full of holes; simple and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant shared-property clue; text accurate.

hints.reason: Simba is the lion hero (LION) and is presented during 'Circle of Life' (CIRCLE); the CIRCLE side needs a beat but clicks for anyone who knows The Lion King.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; CIRCLE comes through the song title, which is very well known.

hints.reason: You crack a code (CODE) and crack a safe (SAFE); instantly familiar collocations.

pairs.pair_note: Clean verb collocation pair.

hints.reason: Cool Whip gives COOL and whipped cream gives CREAM; both instantly familiar, and the pairing is neat because Cool Whip imitates whipped cream.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase join that earns its place: instantly familiar and thematically linked.

hints.reason: Eric Clapton is a famous guitarist (GUITAR) and played in the 1960s band Cream (CREAM); the CREAM side is classic-rock knowledge, which the owner accepts.

pairs.pair_note: Classic-rock reference; younger players may not know Cream, but it is a widely known band.

hints.reason: An oasis is a green spot in the DESERT and date palms are the classic oasis tree (DATE); the date side takes a moment but is a familiar image.

pairs.pair_note: Fair scene clue; DATE is the softer side.

hints.reason: Dune's desert planet Arrakis and literal sand dunes give DESERT, and Dune's spice melange gives SPICE; well known thanks to the recent films.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; DESERT has two routes (sand dunes and Arrakis).

hints.reason: The TARDIS is the Doctor's ship in Doctor Who (DOCTOR) and travels through time (TIME); both sides are direct for anyone who knows the show, though some U.S. players will not know the word.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and neat; the only question is U.S. familiarity with TARDIS, which I judge moderate rather than niche.

hints.reason: Puffer jackets are often down-filled (DOWN) and the pufferfish is a FISH; a fresh, satisfying double.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the text correctly says 'often' since some puffers are synthetic.

hints.reason: Washington is on the quarter's front (WASHINGTON) and an eagle was on its back for decades (EAGLE); the eagle side relies on memory of older coins but is widely remembered.

pairs.pair_note: Text correctly limits the eagle to older designs; DOLLAR would also fit but is no better.

hints.reason: The back of the one-dollar bill shows an unfinished pyramid (PYRAMID) topped by an eye in a triangle (EYE); a familiar, satisfying image.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; text accurate.

hints.reason: A peacock fans out its showy train (FAN) of eye-spotted feathers (FEATHER); clear and vivid.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; strictly the train is upper tail coverts rather than true tail feathers, but 'tail' is standard everyday usage and I did not flag it.

hints.reason: Gravity is a fundamental FORCE and acts through a gravitational FIELD; the field side is school-physics knowledge, a bit flat but fair.

pairs.pair_note: Acceptable; MAGNETIC would fit equally well and is no clear improvement.

hints.reason: A dud is a firework that fails to go off (FIREWORKS) and a lemon is a dud car (LEMON); the synonym route for LEMON gives a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good use of the slang sense of lemon.

hints.reason: A poppy is a FLOWER and Poppy is the heroine of DreamWorks' Trolls films (TROLL); a fun pop-culture double.

pairs.pair_note: Trolls is a big family franchise; text accurate.

hints.reason: Sonic's sidekick Tails gives TAIL by name and is a two-tailed fox (FOX); Tails is mainstream thanks to the games and recent films, though the FOX side needs character knowledge.
hints.fix: FOX: Sonic's sidekick Tails is a young fox.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate; FOX line should mention Sonic so it links the hint, not just the character.

hints.reason: A psychic medium contacts ghosts (GHOST) and medium is the size after small (SMALL); a crisp, delightful double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: Midas turned everything he touched to GOLD, and the Midas touch means a knack for making money (RICH).
hints.fix: RICH: Someone who makes money from everything they try is said to have the Midas touch.

pairs.pair_note: Sound route; the RICH line slightly misstates the idiom (it means a money-making knack, not simply being rich).

hints.reason: Hard-boiled (HARD) and soft-boiled (SOFT) eggs are instantly familiar, and the opposite pairing makes it satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase join that works because the two phrases are a natural pair.

hints.reason: Night at the Museum gives NIGHT and its natural history museum (and history museums generally) gives HISTORY; familiar and neat.

pairs.pair_note: Strong film clue; text accurate (American Museum of Natural History).

hints.reason: A triangle is a percussion INSTRUMENT and a three-sided SHAPE; easy but genuinely two-sided.

pairs.pair_note: Category-style pair; TRIANGLE is the natural best answer.

hints.reason: A map has a KEY (legend) and a SCALE; it sidesteps the obvious music route and lands a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good; MUSIC or PIANO would also fit, but MAP is the more interesting route.

hints.reason: Hedwig is Harry's snowy OWL who delivers his mail (LETTER); widely known Harry Potter detail.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; text accurate.

hints.reason: Caesar was killed on the Ides of MARCH, in ROME; famous history with a satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; text accurate (44 BC, Shakespeare's soothsayer).

hints.reason: Star Trek's Vulcans do the mind meld (MIND) and volcano is named after Vulcan, the Roman fire god (VOLCANO); two indirect routes with a strong aha.

pairs.pair_note: My favourite of the batch; both facts are true and both routes are familiar pop-culture/classical knowledge.

hints.reason: An octopus has suction cups (OCTOPUS) and a vacuum cleaner works by suction (VACUUM); a pleasant property link.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; text accurate.

hints.reason: Neverland is home to Captain Hook's PIRATE crew and is where Peter Pan stays YOUNG forever; a lovely story clue.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; better than HOOK, which would not reach YOUNG.

hints.reason: Radio signals travel as radio waves (RADIO) and surfers ride ocean waves (SURFING); clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair double meaning.

hints.reason: ABBEY gives ROAD instantly via Abbey Road, but ZEBRA depends on knowing the British term 'zebra crossing' for the cover's crosswalk, which many U.S. players will not reach unaided even if it clicks once explained.
hints.fix: ROAD: Abbey Road is both the Beatles album and the London street shown on its cover.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely once explained and the facts are right; the verdict hinges on U.S. familiarity with 'zebra crossing' and could reasonably be PASS for a Beatles-aware audience.

hints.reason: WIND completes windshield (SHIELD) and windscreen (SCREEN), the same car part in U.S. and British English; windscreen is also used in the U.S. for motorcycles and microphones, so it is widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase join with a neat 'same object, two names' twist; british_only is a familiarity note only.

hints.reason: A spade is a digging tool like a SHOVEL and spades is a card SUIT; the synonym side is honest and the suit side gives the aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning; text accurate.

hints.reason: A mole is a dark spot on the skin (SPOT) and an undercover informant inside an organization (SPY); a crisp double meaning that also avoids the obvious animal sense.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning; text accurate.
